Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
- 29-year-old woman with 2-month history of work-related anxiety, poor sleep, palpitations, and low mood seeking advice.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Progressive anxiety over last ~2 months since starting new retail head-office job; dreads leaving house for work.
- Associated symptoms: Morning palpitations (irregular, lasting minutes–10 min), racing heart before waking alarm, difficulty initiating sleep (3–4 h total), early waking, fatigue, anhedonia, avoidance of social and recreational activities. Appetite largely unchanged except increased chocolate intake. No panic attacks. No suicidal ideation.
- Pertinent negatives: No prior similar episodes; no illicit drug use; no chest pain except awareness/discomfort when heart races.
- Past medical history: Not reported.
- Medications: None mentioned.
- Allergies: Not documented.
- Family history: Mother with past depression.
- Social history: Lives with parents. Alcohol—heavy drinking most Fridays/Saturdays (exceeds recommended limits) plus occasional weekday wine. Occasional smoker. No recreational drugs.
- Preventive care: Not discussed.

Examination:
- Vitals: not recorded.
- Physical exam: none documented.

Impression:
- Work-related generalized anxiety with secondary insomnia and low mood; palpitations likely anxiety-related but basic medical causes to be excluded.

Plan:
- Provide NHS IAPT self-referral link for one-to-one talking therapy (CBT).
- Share online anxiety and sleep-hygiene resources for immediate use.
- Order basic blood tests (not specified) to evaluate palpitations; patient to phone support line to arrange.
- Schedule GP follow-up one week after blood tests to review results and clinical progress.
- Advise patient to contact GP sooner if anxiety worsens or daily functioning further impaired; medication may be considered if non-pharmacologic measures insufficient.

Quality checks:
● Missing/expected elements: allergies, full medication list, past medical history, vital signs, physical exam findings.
● Internal conflicts: Patient initially denies chest pain but later describes pain when heart is beating fast—minor discrepancy (conflict noted).
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; occasional filler words, no inaudible sections.
